figure1:
Use case: scientific-educational / photorealistic conceptual cover.
Create an entirely new, visually stunning panoramic academic-paper teaser for a robotics deformable simulation platform, named exactly "DeformLabSim". Landscape aspect ratio about 2.4:1, as high resolution as possible. This is conceptual platform artwork, not measured simulation evidence. A cohesive cinematic scene fills the whole composition: a sophisticated realistically modeled sunlit robotics workroom with stone workbench, brushed-metal clamps, warm wood, soft global illumination, subtle architectural context. A beautifully engineered white seven-joint research robot with plausible parallel gripper stretches a large teal woven fabric from a fixed metal clamp. Make the cloth a visually dominant sculptural form, with believable taut regions, folds, curl and tiny fabric fibers, not a plain polygon or plastic sheet. The other end remains visibly anchored to the tabletop fixture. Frame the full robot and both cloth attachment points, with the cloth suspended prominently across the center. A small second example of a yellow soft volumetric block being visibly squeezed by a robot gripper can appear in a carefully framed right-side detail window. Use photographic material realism and elegant restrained scientific graphic design, not sci-fi and not a generic dashboard. Across the bottom, integrate a narrow aligned strip of four visually rich task vignettes with subtly rounded borders: compressed teal soft block between fingers; real woven cloth in a friction clamp; cloth folding over itself on a fixture; two deformable blocks contacting. Render all four as clear 3D conceptual scenes consistent with the main environment. Tiny restrained captions respectively "Soft-body manipulation", "Cloth gripping", "Cloth folding", "Multi-body contact". The main large title "DeformLabSim" appears in clean elegant white or deep navy typography on suitable negative space near the upper left; below it the short subtitle "Contact-aware simulation for visual manipulation". Maintain clean reading hierarchy and generous separation between the hero and the task strip. Use warm-neutral realistic background, saturated teal fabric, restrained yellow accents and slate-blue secondary elements. No fake experimental plots, no performance numbers, no UI screenshots, no logos of other companies, no huge block diagram, no geometric cubes pretending to be cloth. The visual should feel like the gorgeous full-width teaser of a top computer-vision/robotics paper, strong scene depth, attractive lighting, close enough to see physical interaction.
figure2:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create a wide, extremely clean academic physics-runtime architecture diagram for DeformLabSim. Landscape panoramic 3:1 ratio. White background, refined Times-like readable serif labels, restrained pastel yellow, sage green, slate blue and teal scientific palette. Use beautiful miniature 3D rendered physical objects, tetrahedral mesh cutaways, contact-node markers, slim grey arrows. This is conceptual schematic artwork. Not a screenshot and no fabricated charts.
Four horizontally arranged numbered stages spanning the FULL width, with approximately 20%, 40%, 20%, 20% width:
"01 Task inputs" shows a miniature white robot gripper, a teal tetrahedral soft block, a small folded fabric swatch, material swatches. Labels "Geometry + materials" and "Actions".
"02 Native solve + selective contact" is the central dominant stage inside one light dashed enclosure. It shows a teal deformable VOLUMETRIC block compressed by a robot gripper on a finite rigid support, a tetrahedral cutaway inside the block, yellow highlighted contact boundary nodes. Under that main physical schematic, three small mesh-boundary views connected by arrows: "Discover" then "Retain response" then "Update". Label the small row "Volume contact augmentation". A small looping grey arrow from Update to Discover says "Inner iterations". This mechanism must be depicted on a volumetric block, NOT on cloth. Along the upper edge of the stage, a thin clearly separate bypass arrow labelled "Cloth / multi-body routes" passes toward the state/output stages; cloth is a separate simulation route and must not appear to use the selective volume law.
"03 Consistent state" shows three miniature tetrahedral partition copies mapping by converging arrows to a single physical tetrahedral mesh. Label "Mass-weighted mapping". Below it show clean mathematical text "x, v, d". One small line "Commit physical state".
"04 Synchronized output" shows three neatly aligned miniature scientific icons, no fake photographs: a small camera with an RGB sensor plane, a colorful smooth depth plane, and a teal mesh with pose axes. Labels "RGB-D", "Geometry + poses", "Actions + time".
A thin bottom feedback arrow from stage 03 back toward 01 labelled "Next physics step". Keep all labels spelled correctly, use only specified labels. Plenty of whitespace, no decorative backgrounds, no thick block-box flowchart, no bar graphs. The proportions must be panoramic and readable when printed across both columns of a conference paper.
figure2_final_edit:
Edit this existing architecture diagram. Keep its excellent clean white 3:1 panoramic layout, all four stages, colors, typography, 3D illustrations and overall style. Make these scientific corrections precisely:
1. In the rightmost stage, rename the camera/image-plane row to "RGB"; rename the colored depth-field row to "Depth"; rename the bottom tetrahedral mesh + axes row to "Geometry + poses". Add "Actions + time" as a small textual output line below these three rows if space permits. Match every label to the correct visual.
2. The key selective contact method acts on the stationary finite support UNDER the soft volumetric block. On the large central compressed-block illustration, remove the yellow dots along the moving gripper fingers and place the yellow contact dots along the underside where the block meets its rigid support. Retain the visibly compressed tetrahedral volume and gripper. In the three small Discover / Retain response / Update illustrations, place marked boundary nodes along each block's bottom contact face, not its vertical side. A thin grey finite support beneath the mini blocks is appropriate.
3. The upper thin arrow labelled "Cloth / multi-body routes" must clearly bypass the central dashed volume-contact enclosure, connecting task input to state/output, not originate at the gripper.
4. The lower feedback arrow labelled "Next physics step" must originate from stage 03 Consistent state, after "Commit physical state", and return to stage 01 Task inputs; do not start it from the output stage.
No other new objects, no extra words, do not narrow the panoramic aspect. Preserve all other artwork.
